claims.text: The initial Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEA is a multiphase material containing several constituent phases.
An advanced free-energy sampling framework can combine first-principles calculations with kinetic Monte Carlo or molecular-dynamics simulations.
Integrating this framework into thermal-processing design will enable predictive control of phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Framework-guided processing will increase the fraction of targeted phases.
Framework-guided processing will reduce the formation of undesired phases.
The free-energy landscape can be systematically mapped as a function of annealing temperature, cooling rate, and pressure.
The mapped free-energy landscape can be used to tailor heat-treatment protocols.
Processing-induced changes in the free-energy landscape modulate nucleation sites.
Processing-induced changes in the free-energy landscape alter phase-boundary configurations.
Modulation of nucleation sites and phase boundaries directs phase transformations.
Mapping the free-energy landscape predicts the thermodynamic driving forces for nucleation and growth of different phases.
Mapping the free-energy landscape predicts kinetic barriers to nucleation and growth of different phases.
Adjusting processing conditions according to predicted driving forces and barriers can favor desired phases.
Adjusting processing conditions according to predicted driving forces and barriers can suppress unwanted phase-transformation pathways.
Framework-guided processing will outperform conventional empirical thermal treatments in desired-phase enrichment and suppression of unwanted secondary phases.
HEAs exhibit thermodynamic and kinetic complexities associated with their multicomponent nature.
Diffusion kinetics may limit the accuracy or performance of the proposed free-energy-guided approach in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Local compositional fluctuations may introduce complexities not captured by the modeled free-energy landscape.
The quantitative prediction of nucleation kinetics and phase-fraction changes requires calibration against experiments.
